content.text:
### Two inputs, one transcription response
Treat lactose availability and glucose availability as separate inputs. Lactose can remove repression through its inducer; low glucose supports activation. Predict each input's effect before predicting their combined output. This qualitative model describes regulation, not a literal digital on/off switch.

Reference: [OpenStax: prokaryotic gene regulation](https://openstax.org/books/biology/pages/16-2-prokaryotic-gene-regulation).

### Coordinated transcription
The E. coli lac operon groups genes involved in lactose metabolism under shared transcriptional control.

### Repression at the operator
Without inducer, the lac repressor binds the operator and suppresses transcription.

### Lactose relieves repression
Allolactose derived from lactose binds the lac repressor and reduces its operator binding.

content.text:
Induction changes regulatory protein activity and transcription without requiring a new DNA sequence. Basal expression and transport make the real system more nuanced than a binary switch. Regulation can be reversible as conditions change.

### Glucose-sensitive activation
In the standard lac operon model, low glucose favours cAMP-CAP activation of transcription.

### Combining the two signals
In the standard model, lac expression is high when lactose is present and glucose is low: repression is relieved and CAP activation is available.

### Derepression is not full activation
With lactose and abundant glucose, lac repression can be relieved while CAP activation remains weak, producing lower expression than under low glucose.

arguments.question: Which condition favours high lac expression in this model?
arguments.explanation: The inducer relieves repression and low glucose favours CAP activation.
